reviewed_assertions: tests/test_drain_week_view.py:65 checks the fixture size and fails if its construction stops yielding 120 requests; it is fixture validation rather than a product regression guard.

tests/test_drain_week_view.py:96-137 uses literal hand counts, reason counts, rates and estimates; dropping a phase split, misclassifying a held reason, omitting a recent launch or landing, or changing the denominator reddens a corresponding assertion.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:130-132 reads two differently ordered verdict entries and fails if the older entry wins.

tests/test_drain_week_view.py:133-135 fails if ordinary pending upstream waits are listed as stuck, while :180-185 fails if the satisfied ready wait is omitted or its verdict is wrong; neither checks a failed upstream that should advance to blocked-upstream.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:160-172 asserts admission's existing resolver against literal queued and awaiting-upstream outcomes, validating the fixture independently of the new drain result.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:214-216 fails if a landed request launched in the last day is counted from its two-day-old dispatch stamp or if its landing is omitted.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:223 fails if a zero landing rate produces any estimate or a division error.
tests/test_drain_week_view.py:237-241 fails if MCP omits either half of the 500 pointers or either cold or warm call reaches 30 seconds.
No added assertion compares the drain result with the same value supplied to the code under test; expected counts and phases are independent literals.
